title: Voice and video call setup
like: the ringing part of a calling app or phone carrier
brief: People tap a name and expect the other phone to ring in a second or two. Your job is the setup: find where the person is, ring their devices and connect the two sides. Everyone calls at the same moments, like evenings and holidays.

clarify.q: Do you carry the voice itself?
clarify.a: No. Voice and video flow between the phones or a media service. You only set the call up and tear it down.

clarify.q: How fast must a call ring?
clarify.a: About 2 seconds from the tap. Longer feels broken.

clarify.q: What if a data centre fails?
clarify.a: Calls already in progress should continue. New calls must find another route quickly.

notes: Setting up one call takes about 8 small messages (approx.).
About 1,900 calls begin each second at the evening peak (approx.).

hints: To ring someone you must know which server holds their open connection. Where can that be kept?
Phones keep a live connection. A fast store maps each person to their connection, and a pub/sub channel carries the ring to it.
Call signaling has validity deadlines; old setup requests are not useful durable work. Measure the failed boundary, waiting time and retry work before choosing a change.

editorial.summary: Phones hold a live connection to a gateway. A presence store remembers which gateway each person is on, and a pub/sub channel carries ring and answer messages to it. Spreading across zones means one failure only costs the calls on that zone.

designs.name: Live gateways and a presence map
designs.why: Signaling servers stay stateless. They look up where a person is in the presence store, then ring the gateway that holds that connection directly. History is written to SQL afterwards, off the ringing path.

tradeoffs: Keeping presence in a fast store makes ringing quick, but it may briefly say a person is online after they left.
Running in several regions keeps calls quick for everyone, at the price of more machines and a harder failover plan.
Sending the voice directly between phones is cheap, but some networks block it, so a relay service is needed as backup.
Retrying a ring is kind to flaky phones, but it must not make a phone ring twice.
editorial.realWorld: Calling apps handle many millions of live connections and set up thousands of calls a second at peak. Calls cluster around evenings and holidays (approx.).
